To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ClC‐3 is a 2Cl−: 1H+ exchangers, with an anion selectivity sequence of I− > Br− > Cl− > F− > SCN− > NO3− > SO4−.

the ClC‐3 chloride/proton exchanger is an efficient transporter that cycles between a “coupled” and “uncoupled” state, that the glutamate gate (E224) and tyrosine gate (Y572) act in concert to regulate transport, gating, and coupling, and that the ClC family members are not only chloride channels, but also chloride/proton exchangers that are regulated by the same gates that control chloride permeation.

ClC‐3 is a bidirectional anion/proton exchanger with an exchange ratio of 2Cl−:1H+, but with a low efficiency of transport; the outer and central gates are anion barriers, which contribute to the voltage dependence of gating, and interact to maintain coupling during cycling; protonation of the outer gate inhibits ClC‐3 activity, and the central tyrosinate gate is essential for anion selectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and regulation of the chloride channel family of ClC proteins.
the structure, mechanism and regulation of ClC chloride channels.
understanding how ClC channels transport ions, and with understanding the structure‐function relationships of these important proteins.

the ClC‐3 ClC‐2/1H+ transporter has been studied in great detail, and the results are consistent with a ClC‐2‐type transporter that exchanges 2 Cl− ions for 1 H+ ion, with the anion selectivities of the inner and outer anion selectivity filters being determined by the presence and absence of the Y572 –OH group, respectively.
ClC‐3, ClC‐5, ClC‐6 and ClC‐7 are all proton–chloride exchangers.
ClC‐3, ClC‐5, ClC‐7, and ClC‐2 are exchangers.

E224 and Y573 are essential for ClC‐3 function, that they act as anion selectivity barriers, and that the Y573 side chain and – OH are important for the voltage dependence of Q movement and for coupling.
the proton‐mediated ClC‐3 Cl−/H+ exchange is a highly regulated process.
the proton‐dependent anion exchanger ClC‐3 has evolved to maintain endosome pH and [Cl−], and that the anion selectiviy filter is a major determinant of ClC‐2 gating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ClC‐3 Cl‐/H+ antiporter couples ion fluxes through a complex network of gates that are sensitive to both internal and external pH.

ClC‐3 is a 2Cl‐/1H+ transporter that couples Cl‐ transport to endosome acidification, and the gating of this channel is controlled in part by the protonation of residues within the selectivity filter.
the gating of ClC‐5 is more tightly controlled by the cytosolic pH and the anion permeability of the pore.
